key_insight: Complete procedural specifications—not the skill format itself—accounted for most gains in AI agents’ agreement with reference clinical EHR derivations.
clinical_relevance: Explicit rules for codes, time windows, missingness, and output granularity may improve reproducibility of EHR research variables, but agent outputs still require validation.
method: Benchmarked 28 clinical derivation tasks across 15 task families on MIMIC-IV and eICU.
Compared clinician-reviewed skills with no skills, operational specifications, decoy skills, and reference SQL.
Tested schema changes and conducted a descriptive replication with Claude Code.
evidence_signal: In Codex evaluation, skills increased reward by 0.136, with 26 of 28 tasks improving; only 25 of 280 with-skill runs passed every strict check, versus 13 of 280 without skills.
watch_item: Higher reward reflected partial reference agreement, not reliable task completion; skills barely improved which rows agents returned.
paper_title: M4Bench: Evaluating Procedural Specification for Clinical EHR Derivation Agents
